## Result

Request 4 is **not publicly downloadable at present**, but it is **requestable for research/reproduction** through the Smithsonian Archives of American Art. The blocker is therefore no longer uncertainty about the folder's existence or location; it is an archive-access / digitization-order step.

Target confirmed:

- Collection: **Jim Sanborn papers, circa 1945-2024**
- Repository: **Archives of American Art, Smithsonian Institution**
- Series: **Series 3 — Commission Files**
- Kryptos subgroup: **"Kryptos" CIA Headquarters**
- Container: **Box 6, Folder 10**
- Folder title: **Pre-Production and Notes, 1990-1999**
- Record ID: **AAA.sanbojim_ref75**
- GUID: `https://n2t.net/ark:/65665/mw959ceddbd-7991-4d67-ad7a-cb676e443e98`
- AAA folder page: `https://www.aaa.si.edu/collections/jim-sanborn-papers-22298/series-3/box-6-folder-10`
- Smithsonian object page: `https://www.si.edu/object/archives/components/sova-aaa-sanbojim-ref75`

The AAA folder page currently says the image assets have **not been fully processed** and gives **No downloads available**. It offers two routes instead: request an appointment in the Washington, D.C. reading room, or request a reproduction.

## Why the folder remains high-value

The Series 3 scope note says the commission files contain project applications, contracts, **designs and sketches**, budgets, **some photographs**, correspondence, **notes**, type-work quotes, related research, project concepts, and public-art contracts. The same Kryptos subgroup also contains:

- Box 6 Folder 8 — `Sculpture, 1993-2009`
- Box 6 Folder 9 — `Book, undated`
- Box 6 Folder 10 — `Pre-Production and Notes, 1990-1999`
- Box 6 Folder 11 — `Codes Research, circa 1980s-circa 2002`
- Box 6 Folder 12 — `Dedication, 1990`
- Box 6 Folder 18 — `Cracked Codes and Charts, 1990-circa 2013`

For the present project, Folder 10 remains the best single first request because it could contain fabrication/layout evidence without requiring speculative cryptanalysis. Folder 11 may be valuable later, but it also carries greater contamination risk because its title explicitly concerns codes research.

## Digitization / reproduction route

Archives of American Art's current reproduction instructions say researchers can select a folder in the finding aid and use **Request Reproduction**, which routes to the Smithsonian Aeon research-request system.

For **Collection Folder and Oral History Transcript Photoduplication**, AAA currently lists:

- Use: personal, research, and classroom use; not for reproduction/duplication
- Price: **$40 per folder**
- Deliverable: **PDF**
- Maximum: 10 folders per order

AAA's Digitization on Demand page says it will deliver a PDF of the full contents of requested folders, generally **within six weeks of payment** when new scanning is required. Eligibility remains subject to curatorial approval, physical condition, donor restrictions, Smithsonian policy, and copyright restrictions. Some oversized, fragile, bound, slide/negative, or otherwise special materials can require different handling or charges.

Current official service pages:

- Reproductions: `https://www.aaa.si.edu/services/reproductions`
- Digitization on Demand: `https://www.aaa.si.edu/services/digitization-on-demand`
- Ask a Reference Question: `https://www.aaa.si.edu/services/questions`
- Reference Services phone: **202-633-7950**
- Washington, D.C. research center: 750 9th Street NW, Victor Building, Suite 2200, Washington, DC 20001

## Exact recommended request

Request **one folder only first**:

> Jim Sanborn papers, Series 3 — Commission Files, "Kryptos" CIA Headquarters, Box 6, Folder 10, `Pre-Production and Notes, 1990-1999`.

Research purpose should be described narrowly as historical/fabrication research on the public Kryptos sculpture, especially:

- cipher-panel line layout and row starts
- character spacing / pitch / kerning
- punch or type templates
- fabrication or shop drawings
- pre-production diagrams
- notes naming a public key source, physical indexing mechanism, or layout rule

Do **not** ask the archive to identify, summarize, or expose any alleged K4 solution/plaintext. The project contamination rule still applies.

## What not to infer

The Smithsonian catalog metadata does not establish that Folder 10 contains a key, cipher method, or usable panel drawing. It establishes only that the folder exists within the Kryptos commission files and is available through research/reproduction channels. No cryptanalytic conclusion changes until the actual contents are inspected.

K4 remains unsolved.
